title: ::: K-IG 교육 영어듣기훈련프로그램 | 기초2 | 제 001 회 강의 :::
label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 129 ]

blocks.text: Changes in the water systems of buildings can also lead to disease. In the 1970s, there was a worldwide shortage of oil. To save energy, many buildings lowered the temperature of their hot water. Water that is warm but not hot is just right for a deadly germ called Legionella. The germ also grows in the water of air-conditioning cooling towers, and people become infected when they breathe in tiny drops of that water in mist or spray. In 1976, more than 180 people who had stayed at or visited a hotel in Philadelphia became ill, and 29 of them died.
